children: Chicago wheat and corn futures fell to three-month lows on Wednesday as an advancing US harvest, renewed diplomatic efforts to end Russia's war with Ukraine and technical selling weighed on prices.
The most-traded wheat contract on the Chicago Board of Trade
fell 13-3/4 cents to $6.29-1/2 a bushel by 12:16 p.m. CT (1716 GMT). Most-active soybeans

New talks between the US and Russia to end Russia's war with Ukraine dampened grain prices, said Arlan Suderman, chief commodities economist at StoneX. The discussions raised expectations of potential de-escalation that might revive grain shipments through the critical shipping area.
Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted US envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday, a day after Witkoff met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in Norway.
An advancing US harvest encouraged investment funds to liquidate long positions built up in recent months when grain markets rallied to multiyear highs.

Dry weather forecast across the Midwest this week is expected to let US farmers accelerate harvesting of what the government projects to be bumper corn and soybean crops. Showers last week left harvest progress below market expectations.
Harvest supplies have overshadowed renewed Chinese demand for US soybeans, as the US Department of Agriculture confirmed more purchases on Tuesday.
In Brazil, farmers had planted 26% of the projected area of their 2026/27 soybean crop as of last Thursday, agribusiness consultancy AgRural said on Monday.
